- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast or apply downward bias to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); apply lagged correction: subtract 0.5–1.0 from forecast 2–3 days after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 0.3–0.7 to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price peaks in late period (last 7–10 days); apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5 to final 5–7 forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/– values), model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast variance or add 0.2–0.5 to mid-range values.
